source.title: Gradient Descent Maximizes the Margin of Homogeneous Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied. The extracted text includes figure and table material; no apparent cutoff.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a measured network property—normalized margin—changes during standard training and tracks test performance, using margin and accuracy measurements rather than directly testing the catalog’s gap predictors.
record.gate_note: Reports training and test accuracy alongside margin during extended training, and robustness outcomes. Theoretical results about separable homogeneous networks are not empirical generalization-gap measurements. Figure-only accuracy and robustness curves are not converted into precise values; cited prior-work findings are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study tests implicit normalized-margin growth and input robustness, neither of which is a claim version here. It does not measure magnitude-aware weight sharpness or compare generalization-gap predictors for V7. Its random-label fitting statement cites Zhang et al.; its own experiments do not test V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate but needs a convergence qualification. Under the stated homogeneity, separability, loss, regularity, and learning-rate assumptions, a smoothed normalized margin is nondecreasing, and every limit point of the normalized parameter direction is along a KKT point of the margin problem. The theory does not guarantee convergence of the parameter direction or a globally maximal margin; discrete-gradient-descent results require smoothness. Experiments show increased normalized margins and threshold-dependent L2 robustness gains, with only slight changes in test accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Studies implicit margin regularization and margin/robustness during prolonged training; it does not directly compare training error with test error as a function of the claim’s listed conditions or measure V7’s sharpness construct.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning-rate schedule changes the speed of training-loss reduction and normalized-margin growth; constant learning rate yields slower margin growth than the loss-based schedule.

fits_no_version.finding: Normalized margins grow substantially during prolonged training, while MNIST CNN and CIFAR-10 VGGNet test accuracy changes only slightly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing normalized training margin through longer training need not substantially improve held-out accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Across the five MNIST checkpoints, normalized margin rises from 5.65e-5 to 1.18e-3, training accuracy remains 100%, and test accuracy is 99.3%, 99.3%, 99.3%, 99.2%, and 99.1%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this MNIST CNN, continued training after perfect training accuracy increases normalized margin without improving test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Later MNIST checkpoints generally improve measured L2 robust accuracy; test curves nearly overlap below epsilon 0.2, and final-checkpoint gains over intermediate checkpoints are marginal or absent in some ranges.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Longer training with loss-based learning-rate scheduling can improve input robustness, depending on the perturbation threshold and evaluation split.

record.problems: The empirical training and test accuracy trajectories are shown as plots without exact accuracy values. Test accuracy is reported at five MNIST checkpoints for one CNN, with no uncertainty estimates. The CIFAR-10 accuracy trajectory is only plotted. Robustness curves are figure-only, and the paper notes improvements can be marginal or nonexistent in some ranges.
record.rows_left_out: No separately stated numerical results for the other learning-rate settings are given. Robustness curve points and detailed loss/margin trajectories in figures were not extracted as exact values; cited prior-work results were excluded.

untested.parts: No own comparison of fitting and held-out accuracy under natural versus random labels.
No width sweep beyond the width needed for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison or locality intervention.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison; loss-based scheduling is not such a comparison.
No batch-size comparison under fixed or adapted training budgets.
No dropout or joint dropout–weight-decay intervention.
No magnitude-aware weight sharpness, correlation with generalization gaps, or comparison of predictor rankings. Normalized margin and input robustness measure different constructs.
No memorization-based example removal and retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: No listed version is tested, so no version-level verdict is warranted. The slight accuracy decline does not challenge V2, which concerns increasing width, or V7, which concerns weight sharpness. No additional version-relevant results require missing rows.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare fitting natural labels with fitting random labels.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
Measures normalized margin, not magnitude-aware sharpness or perturbation tolerance; no ranking against norm- or margin-based measures.
